readinessGate.rule: Implementation may start only when readiness.complete is true and readiness.missing is empty.
requiredFields: security, permissions, rollback, and operator decisions

initiatives.title: Project Intelligence
initiatives.summary: Detect the repository's real stack and conventions before planning, gating, or editing.

initiatives.title: Provider-neutral Workflow Orchestrator
initiatives.summary: Split the flagship workflow into bounded contracts with evidence handoffs and provider adapters.

initiatives.title: Reliability and Release
initiatives.summary: Make the kit testable, portable, packageable, and honest on supported environments.

initiatives.title: Control Plane and Learning
initiatives.summary: Add opt-in distributed operation, privacy-safe learning, and provider parity evidence.

tasks.title: Tracking and readiness foundation
tasks.problem: The post-17 backlog needs one versioned source of truth and a visible fail-closed readiness gate.
examples: When complete, a missing input is shown as needs_input instead of an optimistic percentage.
A malformed or duplicate task ID makes the dashboard fail closed instead of rendering partial progress.

tasks.title: Project Intelligence skill and agent contract
tasks.problem: Fallback assumptions can generate the wrong stack, router, i18n, style, and task structure.
acceptanceCriteria: same repository yields the same normalized profile
unknown and contradictory signals fail closed
no framework is inferred from absence alone
examples: A React Native repository is not scaffolded as a React web application.
A repository without i18n does not receive a fabricated messages.ts completeness gate.

tasks.title: Workflow Orchestrator decomposition contract
tasks.problem: The 2,692-line flagship command couples intake, planning, gates, execution, evidence, and learning into one context-heavy artifact.
acceptanceCriteria: each phase has explicit bounded inputs and outputs
examples: A failed verification phase resumes from the last verified bundle without replaying intake.
A provider action smoke cannot be reported as planning or implementation parity.

tasks.title: Provider-neutral semantic specification model
tasks.problem: Source-specific text leaks into planning and makes equivalent specifications behave differently.
examples: The same acceptance criterion from Confluence or Jira produces the same normalized intent.
An unstated API contract remains unknown instead of being guessed.

tasks.title: Provider-neutral specification adapters
tasks.problem: The kit remains operationally skewed toward Confluence even after runtime URL hardcoding was removed.

missing: approved minimal Jira and Azure DevOps fixture exports

examples: A Jira story and a Confluence page can enter the same planning pipeline.
A missing Jira field is reported, not silently substituted with Confluence assumptions.

tasks.title: Project-derived conditional quality gates
tasks.problem: Static or missing gates either create false failures or miss project-specific regressions.
acceptanceCriteria: only detected systems enable their gates
unknown or conflicting ownership fails closed
examples: A React Router project fails when the feature route is never registered.
A CSS-in-JS project is not forced through an SCSS-only rule.

tasks.title: Phase-aware model selection and routing
tasks.problem: One model setting for every phase hides quality, cost, and latency trade-offs.
examples: A cheap model may summarize intake while a stronger model handles architecture review.
An unavailable vision capability blocks a visual phase instead of silently using text-only output.

tasks.title: Normalized same-input provider parity
tasks.problem: Generated editions and transport smokes do not prove planning or implementation parity.
acceptanceCriteria: same source and constraints are hash-bound
examples: Codex and Copilot can differ in code layout while satisfying the same AC and evidence contract.
A successful click smoke remains transport-only when no planning artifact exists.

tasks.title: Installable distribution bundles
tasks.problem: Copying a private repository is not an installable, versioned product distribution story.
acceptanceCriteria: thin adapters contain no forked business rules
examples: A user installs the Codex plugin instead of copying hidden folders manually.
A Copilot bundle uses the same core schema version as the Claude adapter.

tasks.title: Cross-platform release qualification
tasks.problem: Local Windows fixes exist, but GitHub CI currently proves only Ubuntu.
outOfScope: macOS support claim without a runner
acceptanceCriteria: required Windows and Linux jobs pass
examples: A PowerShell path with spaces works in CI.
A Unix-only date/stat assumption is caught before release.

tasks.title: CLI reliability and direct integration tests
tasks.problem: Large public CLI scripts lack focused malformed-input, I/O, argument, and atomic-output tests.
outOfScope: blanket replacement of every synchronous read
examples: A corrupt feedback log returns a structured error instead of a silent skip.
A KPI output write failure leaves the previous report intact.

tasks.title: Honest isolated-worktree browser verification
tasks.problem: A feature route unavailable from an isolated worktree can be labeled infra-blocked without proving the exact code in a browser.
acceptanceCriteria: browser target is identity-bound to tested worktree
examples: B11 refuses a main-workspace server when the feature exists only in a worktree.
An unavailable route asks for deployment instead of claiming browser verification.

tasks.title: Convention and stack portability audit
tasks.problem: Helpers and templates still contain assumptions from the current Open edX/React target stack.
acceptanceCriteria: generic core imports no Open edX helpers
examples: getHttpClient() is selected only when the project profile proves that convention.
A different data layer is not rewritten into camelCaseObject conventions by default.

tasks.title: Documentation and runtime claim audit
tasks.problem: Documentation, generated editions, and runtime behavior can drift while all files remain syntactically valid.
acceptanceCriteria: critical claims map to executable evidence
examples: A parity-locked claim fails when Copilot output omits a required gate.
A changelog version cannot diverge from the command version silently.

tasks.title: Opt-in distributed control plane
tasks.problem: Multi-repository execution lacks a provider-neutral, least-privilege topology for remote coordination.
acceptanceCriteria: every action is scoped and auditable
examples: A remote worker receives one typed phase envelope, not arbitrary shell access.
Repeating a delivery ID cannot execute the phase twice.

tasks.title: Detailed cross-machine progress tracking
tasks.problem: Current tracking does not fully bind task state, provider run, evidence, machine, and retry lineage.
acceptanceCriteria: task state resolves to exact evidence
examples: A dashboard task links to the exact provider run and evidence hash that completed it.
Two machines cannot overwrite each other's retry history.

tasks.title: Privacy-safe specification and usage data criteria
tasks.problem: Learning and evaluation data need explicit minimization, provenance, retention, and tenant boundaries.
examples: A prompt-evolution metric stores the lesson signal without storing the private specification body.
Cross-tenant evidence references are rejected.

tasks.title: Provider-neutral build harness with optional RAG
tasks.problem: Repository discovery and optional retrieval need a measured boundary so stale or injected context cannot override deterministic facts.
outOfScope: RAG as an authority over repository state
examples: A stale indexed router rule cannot override the current package and route files.
The workflow still operates offline using repository discovery only.

tasks.title: Public-release and GitHub adoption readiness
tasks.problem: A private internal repository lacks the documentation, governance, CI cadence, and adoption surface expected for wider distribution.
examples: An external evaluator can understand installation and contribution without internal Confluence access.
No public artifact is emitted while the operator keeps the distribution private.

tasks.title: Credential lifecycle adapter
tasks.problem: Playwright authentication can expire mid-run, but generic refresh logic is unsafe because auth flows are project-specific.

missing: project-specific refresh capability fixture and security approval

acceptanceCriteria: mid-run expiry has a structured outcome
examples: An expiring token is refreshed only through a project-provided adapter.
A project without refresh support receives needs_input instead of guessed authentication calls.

tasks.title: Self-improvement drift, bias, and evolution tracking
tasks.problem: A successful N-to-N+1 cycle does not by itself prove long-term drift control or representative learning data.
acceptanceCriteria: golden drift stays within approved budget
prompt changes are provenance-bound and reversible
examples: Five refund-processing runs cannot rewrite a rule used by unrelated feature classes.
A regression against the golden set rolls back the proposed evolution.

tasks.title: Distributed Control Panel UI and Remote Operations Console
tasks.problem: The roadmap has control-plane and tracking contracts but no real operator UI that proves authorized remote work from browser intent through worker execution and evidence return.
outOfScope: mock or static UI counted as completion
raw secret or private specification display

missing: completed P17-014 topology and versioned Control Plane API/event contract
completed P17-015 machine/task/run/evidence and retry-lineage model
approved Control Panel information architecture and accessibility acceptance
disposable least-privilege remote worker and bounded execution fixture
content-addressed evidence adapter and quarantine behavior
approved network-separated or two-node E2E topology
inputs: dashboard auth and admin allowlist model

acceptanceCriteria: the authenticated Control Panel renders authoritative machine/task/run/progress/evidence identity from the live Control Plane
approve/cancel/retry are enforced server-side by RBAC and rejected actions have zero execution side effects plus an audit decision
one E2E flow proves Control Panel to Control Plane to disposable remote worker to bounded execution to content-addressed evidence and back to the rendered terminal state without mock substitution
leases, retries, cancellation races, duplicate delivery, stale versions, and late events remain idempotent and monotonic
offline/degraded/unauthorized/quarantined-evidence states are explicit and never displayed as success
sensitive and cross-tenant values are excluded while keyboard, screen-reader, responsive, and accessibility acceptance passes
tests: multi-process Control Plane and worker integration
Playwright exact-dashboard-server E2E with a real disposable worker
in-app browser route and semantic-state corroboration
examples: An approver authorizes a queued task in /control-plane, one least-privilege worker executes the typed envelope, and the same run and evidence hash appear in the terminal Control Panel state.
A viewer or stale approver cannot trigger work; duplicate retry or forged evidence is rejected, audited, and never shown as a successful run.
